en: Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One.
O Lotus-hand, Lotus-seated One,
Lord of the Lotus, Subduer of the Lord of Demons, Vajra-wielder!
I bow to the stainless lotus-feet of the Sage, the lord of the Daityas,
Dānavas, humans, serpents, and the serpent-throne;
his crown is adorned with the radiance of jewels that are fanned by swarms of bees.
Beautiful with auspicious marks that inspire confidence in the abode of Kamalā,
his radiant splendor surpassing the lovely golden lotus;
born after a long time, he was bowed to by his father, the king.
I bow to the stainless lotus-feet of the sinless Sage,
who is saluted by the Lord of the Night (the Moon) and the Lord of the Day (the Sun),
who purifies all people who worship him, and who bestows the desired happiness upon those who seek it.
I bow to the stainless lotus-feet of the Sage, honored by the lotuses that naturally rise from the surface of the earth;
he who sits upon a seat formed at the foot of the tree beneath the elephant-throne, and who grants fearlessness.
I bow to the one established in the meditative concentration of the seat of victory,
whose fourfold energy is firm; who, while the sun was still shining,
has conquered and lowered the banner of Namuci, and has brought his power to an end.
O you who are ever-arisen with beloved speech, who have conquered the battle against Death,
who by the power of the ten perfections caused the earth— the bearer of the mountains—
to tremble; O Girimekhala, best of elephants, whose feet are bowed to by your head!
I bow to Him who is celebrated by the worlds of men and gods,
whose heart was rendered exceedingly pure through the destruction of all taints,
and who subsequently made known the entire range of objects within the scope of the intellect.
I bow to the unconquered, peerless Sage, the Arhat, whose conduct transcends the three worlds and who has made them his object;
his face resembles a lotus frequented by honey-bees and possesses soft, beautiful speech.
I bow to the foremost of sages, who is free from fear and sin,
whose pair of eyes resembles the petals of a beautiful, broad lotus,
and whose stainless forehead shines like the rising orb of the sun.
Lovely with dark-blue cloud-like, curled, soft, and wavy locks of hair;
blazing with a mass of immeasurable radiance spread throughout the interior of the world;
beautiful with the graceful gait of one intoxicated with passion like a rutting elephant;
I bow to that peerless bull among sages, the bestower of the deathless,
whose words are nectar to the ears, permeated with the essence of compassion,
resounding with a hundredfold melodies of praise, and filling the world with his glory.
I bow to him whose face is like the orb of the risen, stainless moon;
the abode of a mass of glory possessing excellent and beautiful marks;
the moon to the lily pond of the minds of those worthy of discipline.
I bow to him who is free from abode, who has transcended all states of existence,
and who is devoid of blemish— he who is like a hundred-rayed sun that dries up the river of craving,
who is untainted by darkness or defilements, who is cultivated by sages, who is clearly perceived, and who bestows happiness.
To him who has dispelled all fears and terrors, who is the refuge for those come for protection,
who bestows the bliss of agelessness and deathlessness, whose compassion is never withdrawn,
and whose well-established feet are served by the assembly of lay disciples; to him [I pay homage].
I bow to Him whose supreme feet remove all harm,
whose entire stainless heart is filled with the nectar of compassion,
who has accomplished immeasurable welfare for the people, and who is compassionate toward the world.
I bow to that sinless Sage, whose feet are served by hundreds of lords of the earth, who is skilled in destroying all evil,
and who subdues the minds of ascetics tormented by both aversion and passion.
I bow down to that supreme deity, the ascetic Gotama,
who has warded off the various sectarian ascetics by his own teaching, and who endures the insults uttered by the multitude of those who hold opposing views.
To the one who has come for refuge, the destroyer of fear, the diamond-throne, the one with hands like lotuses;
to the one intent on ferrying across the immeasurable people fallen into the ocean of existence;
to the one whose head bears the stainless lotus-bud of palms joined in reverence.
I bow to the Sage, the peerless one who has transcended all, who has purified the minds of living beings,
who is free from the taints, the Blessed One who has reached the further shore of existence,
and who constantly bestows the bliss of deathless sovereignty.
O Victor, bowed down by supreme respect and profound veneration,
adorn my head with the dust of your lotus feet;
for the human life-span is as fickle as a tree-leaf shaken by the wind.
O You who bear the weight of compassion, purify my heart— which is stained by craving for existence,
inhabited by a host of unsubdued senses, struck by long-accumulated evil,
and enveloped in unobstructed darkness— making it easy to cross over.
O Victor, you who practiced compassion where there was none, who established order where there was disorder, and who bestowed virtue where there was vice,
and who brought benefit where there was harm— by anyone, anywhere, nothing such as this had ever been done before; yet in you, the compassionate one,
the abode of virtue and the follower of the excellent path, it was performed most perfectly.
O blameless one, whose conduct is beneficial and who dwells in peace, my heart rejoices in you.
Though you have fallen into the peril of existence, you have long practiced the ten perfections,
which indeed consist of walking evenly upon the uneven path.
Day by day and night by night, even in my dreams, my heart constantly delights in you, O Victorious One of noble wisdom, for it is forever compassionate toward you.
You have given what is most difficult to give; you have performed what is most difficult to perform.
"O Treasure of Compassion, peerless in flavor, you have indeed endured that which is exceedingly difficult to bear"—
thus, O Sage, as I recollect your faultless virtues,
my heart delights in you by day, it delights by night; it delights in you constantly.
"You practiced what was exceedingly difficult to practice; you tamed what was exceedingly difficult to tame;
you showed compassion to those who were exceedingly difficult to show compassion toward—truly, you whose heart is devoted to compassion!
O Sage, as I recall these faultless virtues of yours, my heart [is filled with joy]."
He delights by day, he delights by night; he delights constantly in you.
He has traversed what is most difficult to traverse; he has conquered what is most difficult to conquer;
he has endured what is most difficult to endure—truly, with a mind that has attained equanimity.
Thus, O Sage, as I recall your faultless virtues, my heart delights by day and delights by night; it finds constant delight in you.
Even amidst a fire blazing like the most terrible fire of universal destruction, [it remains steadfast].
Having fallen into hell, my mind was long tormented by suffering;
not once did I remember to revere your lotus-like feet.
O Gotama, charioteer of men, forgive this transgression of mine.
Having long followed a conduct unstable in the downward course of rebirths,
with a heart trembling from fear and driven by excessively cruel slaughter,
I did not once remember to resort to your lotus feet, O Father.
Forgive me, O Gotama, supreme among men, for this transgression of mine.
Long devoted to lamentation in the realm of the departed,
I was severely afflicted by hunger and thirst, my belly utterly withered away.
O Father Gotama, supreme among bipeds, I have not once been able to worship your lotus feet; forgive this transgression of mine.
My mind is utterly helpless, corrupted by evil within the realm of Māra.
Born into thick darkness, with a heart long afflicted by extreme suffering,
I did not once remember to worship your lotus feet,
O Father. O Gotama, best among those who dwell, forgive this transgression of mine.
Having long since abandoned that lake of the mind, characterized by excessive evil conduct,
and having thoroughly purified it through tranquility, he entered the state beyond perception;
he did not once even remember to return to those lotus feet of his father to revere them.
Forgive this transgression of mine, O Gotama, bull among sages!
Having become disgusted with the immeasurable evil committed by my own body, you have come here,
having cultivated tranquility and being free from even the slightest fault.
O Father Gotama, elephant among ascetics, forgive this transgression of mine; I was unable even once to revere your lotus feet,
for I am devoid of the Three Jewels and have intensely accumulated great evil.
O Father Gotama, ocean of compassion, forgive this transgression of mine:
that I, born in a foreign land and following a conduct censured by the wise,
have not once before worshipped at Your lotus feet.
If, even among humans, one is born with a defective set of sense faculties,
deformed in body with hands, feet, and so forth, and thus miserable in this world,
one cannot once again resort to your lotus-like feet, O Father.
Forgive this transgression of mine, O Gotama, ocean of wisdom!
I am devoid of the cultivation of intelligence through the proper method, and being obscured,
I am averse to seeing things as they truly are, even regarding wholesome states and the like.
O Father Gotama, lion among men, forgive this transgression of mine; I was unable to worship even once those lotus feet of yours.
For though one may wait for a very long time on earth, such an incomparable moment is difficult to obtain.
O Sage, who brings welfare and happiness to the multitude of gods and humans—
Father, I have not once before worshipped your lotus feet;
O Gotama, best among speakers, forgive this transgression of mine.
With a heart cruel and wicked, prepared for slaughter with sharpened weapons,
delighting in harming others and as terrifying as a brother to Yama,
you did not once remember to take refuge at your father’s lotus feet.
Forgive me, O Gotama, best of sages, for this transgression of mine.
I was intent on seizing the property of others, full of deceit, and devoted to breaking into houses,
waylaying travelers, and committing acts of violence.
O Father, I was not able to worship even once those lotus feet of yours;
O Gotama, bull among sages, forgive this transgression of mine,
for my heart was intoxicated and deluded by the pride of fresh youth.
O Pure One, O Sage, though I loathe it, I am devoted to adultery;
I have not once remembered to worship Your lotus feet, O Father.
O Gotama, forgive this transgression of mine, burdened as You are with compassion.
O King of Men, constantly honored by those devoted to the finest spirits and wines,
yet shunned by the noble and the modest due to your conduct that reaches the highest heights—
you have never once tasted wine, even as you sought to honor your lotus-like feet.
Forgive me, O Gotama, whose taints are destroyed;

this was my transgression. O grandfather of grandfathers, you have lost the immeasurable wealth accumulated by your ancestors, as well as that gathered by your father—a gambler who has ruined his fortune.
I am not able to worship even once those lotus feet of yours, O Father;
O Gotama, conqueror of death, forgive this transgression of mine.
You whose speech is free from falsehood and who brings about the emptiness of what is pleasing to others—
O Gotama, Son of the World, forgive this transgression of mine: though I am skilled in speech, my many words have been fruitlessly harsh,
and I did not once remember to worship your lotus feet.
Coveting the prosperity of others, you were constantly distressed;
intent on non-attachment, you were nowhere seen to experience its fruit.
You did not once remember, O Father, to resort to your own lotus-like feet.
O Gotama, ocean of virtues, forgive this transgression of mine.
That I have repeatedly, for a long time,
acted improperly toward you— whether through my body, my speech, or my mind— has been immeasurable.
Forgive me, O Gotama, you who remove misfortune; [forgive] the many kinds of misdeeds I have committed.
Grant me the auspicious state that is imperishable, deathless, and free from becoming.
[I dwell] in the forest, filled with corpses and shrouded in darkness, feeling revulsion.
My mother’s impurity was my womb, and the multitude of worms was my dwelling;
I lay within the abyss of existence, wandering without refuge.
O Blessed One, be my refuge for crossing over the ocean of becoming!
Going out from the city, I fell upon a path strewn with thorns;
O Healer, you who have made the thorn-seeker’s task easy,
I wandered in the prison of existence, which is without refuge.
O Blessed One, become my refuge in crossing the ocean of existence!
I have fallen outside [the fold], my body tormented by the disease of sensual pleasure;
deprived of wisdom, I am unable even to speak or to understand.
Wandering through the grasp of existence which is without refuge, I have come to you, O Blessed One;
be my refuge for crossing the ocean of existence.
If you are born, may you be happy, beloved by people, and a father to those dear to you.
A fool, delighting in various kinds of play, seized by passion,
I wandered through the grasp of existence which is without refuge.
O Blessed One, be my refuge for crossing over the ocean of existence!
Though young, bound by the shackles of the household, and possessed of wealth,
I was suddenly seized by disease and separated from my beloved wife and children;
wandering in this prison of existence which offers no refuge, I died.
O Blessed One, be my refuge in crossing over the ocean of existence.
Having attained an undecaying body while under the sway of fresh youth,
you are now worn out by old age, yet remain skillful and steadfast in the supreme Dhamma.
Wandering in the unfathomable ocean of existence, I am without refuge;
O Blessed One, may You be my refuge for crossing over the sea of becoming.
Having realized Your body to be healthy, stable, and free from disease, You are perfectly equanimous.
Turning my back on the wholesome, utterly helpless and struck down by the fetters,
I died while wandering in the abyss of existence, O Blessed One, which offers no refuge.
Be my refuge, O Blessed One, for crossing over the ocean of existence.
Having reflected that one's own life is immortal, stable, and free from affliction, the wise man, whose mind is not intoxicated by the pride of life, casts it aside;
for I have wandered through the grasp of existence, which is without refuge, as if it were immortal.
O Blessed One, may you be my refuge for crossing over the ocean of existence.
The lord of the earth was seized while intent on harming others, plundering wealth, and violating the wives of others;
he has been subjected to many executions and imprisonments and struck down.
Wandering through the perilous depths of existence, I am without refuge;
O Blessed One, be my refuge so that I may cross the ocean of becoming.
Having fallen into the waters of hell, I have slipped from the summit of a mountain tree.
Seized by a hunter’s snare and bitten by venomous serpents,
I died while wandering in the abyss of existence, O Lord, where there is no refuge.
O Blessed One, be my refuge to cross over the ocean of becoming.
Afflicted by the rites of malevolent sorcery, seized by nocturnal spirits,
and faltering through the consumption of poisoned food and sudden intoxicants,
I wandered through the prison of existence, O Immortal One, without any refuge.
O Blessed One, may you be my refuge for crossing over the ocean of existence.
You yourself, having become enraged toward your own kin, devoid of wisdom,
and having faltered through immeasurable lapses such as causing the throat of Sivi to wither, [fell into hell].
Wandering in this ocean of existence which is without refuge, I have come to you, O Blessed One;
be my refuge for crossing over the sea of becoming.
Devoted to honoring his father, happy, and beloved by his father—
Devoted to intense mourning for my father’s death,
I wept for a long time in this most difficult and arduous cycle of existence;
O Blessed One, be my refuge in crossing the ocean of worldly becoming!
Supremely devoted to saluting my own mother who had raised me,
and remembering the greatness of her virtues even in death,
I wept for a long time in this most difficult and unbearable prison of existence.
O Blessed One, be my refuge in crossing the ocean of existence. You who are devoted to honoring your teachers and deities,
most dear and gentle of speech, you whose feet were served with devotion,
and who are now deeply pained by the death of your teacher;
For a long time, in this most difficult and painful cycle of existence,
O Blessed One, be my refuge for crossing the ocean of worldly life.
Having abandoned the household life and its wealth, I am now full of delight.
At my death, I wept for a long time with exceeding compassion for my beloved wife, son, and daughter; O Blessed One, in this world-ocean so difficult to endure and full of hardship,
may you be my refuge for crossing over the sea of existence.
At the death of my two sisters, who were dear to me as my elder and younger siblings,
and even at the death of my own kinsmen, friends, and disciples,
I wept for a long time with extreme compassion in this most unbearable and difficult prison of existence.
O Blessed One, be my refuge for crossing the ocean of existence. O Lord of the World,
you are the one who removes the thieves that are the hosts of enemies,
who carries away the waters of the rivers, and who extinguishes the blazing fires of the world.
O Blessed One, my refuge for crossing the ocean of existence, may you be my protector as I have long been here in this abyss of miserable rebirths, with my wealth destroyed.
May you save me who have fallen into the peril of existence, which is exceedingly difficult to traverse and agitated by its unevenness.
Though I have long experienced this calamity as something unbearable and full of fear, my heart,
deceived by a mere fragment of pleasure, has not abandoned its craving for existence;
O Treasury of Compassion, dispel that entire craving of mine.
Just as death has birth as its limit, so too birth has death as its limit;
by both of these, fear alone is certain for me regarding existence.
Yet, there is only that which is auspicious, devoid of both birth and death.
O Blessed One, grant me that auspicious, deathless, and taintless state.
Though my mind has long been ordained for renunciation, it remains unimpeded by craving,
yet it is tormented by the pleasures of existence— alas, it is bound by the age of strife!
From that end, from fear, protect me; may existence be my refuge.
O Blessed One, you are my resort, the crossing over the ocean of existence.
